text:
tara: Heads-up: onboarding canary for cinder-int4 showed a weird structured-output regression — arrays of tool-args are sometimes reordered or duplicated. This breaks our tool-call contract which expects positional args.

kevin: saw that too. low-volume but reproducible on streaming + kv-cache enabled. Can you post numbers?

tara: canary snapshot (N=1200):
- strict-schema pass: 94.6%
- json-parse pass: 99.0%
- semantic-arg-order failures: 3.4%
- duplicate-element in arg arrays: 1.2%

mira: examples?

tara: pasted samples (sanitized):
```
{"tool":"create_event","args":[{"title":"launch"},{"date":"2026-03-01"}]}
// becomes ->
{"tool":"create_event","args":[{"date":"2026-03-01"},{"title":"launch"}]}

{"tool":"rank_items","args":["a","b","b","c"]}
// becomes ->
{"tool":"rank_items","args":["a","b","c"]} // missing duplicate then reordered
```

kevin: ordering should be preserved; routing uses position. Duplicate removal is not intended. Any logs that show where transformation happens?

ops-bot: Collected trace for request id=uu-81: stream-chunks received at t0,t1,t2. kv-cache warm resumed before final chunk. No explicit postprocess called.

mira: hypothesis: streaming chunk boundaries + a late KV cache splice cause the decoder to re-emit tokens from buffered prefix causing both duplicate tokens and mis-ordered concatenation when merges aren't stable. Quantized decoder may be emitting slightly different tokenization that changes chunk split points.

kevin: interesting. If prefix A emitted, then cache resumes and emits A' with slightly different tokenization, naive concatenation could produce duplicated substructures or reorder arrays when model regenerates part of array.

tara: agreed. quick repro: run streaming with artificially small chunk size and force kv warm. Repro reproducible in synthetic harness.

mira: short-term mitigations: 1) disable KV-resume on canary for cinder-int4 (isolate); 2) runtime defensive merge: when reassembling JSON, prefer earlier chunk's array order and forbid dedup/removal heuristics unless explicit; 3) add a schema-aware merge validator that rejects merged JSON if an array element appears to have been shifted.

kevin: we should be careful - forbidding dedup might leave real duplicates from model. But our tool semantics expect exact order. I like schema-aware validation + reject-and-retry rather than silent heal.

ops-bot: quick patch deployed to canary branch: kv-resume disabled for cinder-int4 at 1769999905. Canary updated to 2% traffic.

canary-bot: after patch snapshot (N=400): semantic-arg-order failures dropped to 0.8%, duplicates to 0.3%. Good but not gone.

mira: next steps:
- runtime: add merge validator that replays parse on candidate merged text and compares array lengths and element fingerprints (hash of normalized content). If mismatch, reject merged candidate and trigger full re-eval (non-streaming) for that request.
- eval: expand structured-output test set with arrays and repeated elements to catch this in future onboarding.

kevin: agree. Also add a telemetry metric: merged_array_mismatch_count and kv_resume_triggered_count by model+quant.

tara: i'll open PR for the merge-validator (canary-only for now) and the expanded tests in the eval harness. mira can you prototype the fingerprint function (normalize -> stable-serialize -> sha1) to avoid false positives from whitespace?

mira: on it. small note: fingerprint must be deterministic across unicode normalizations; will normalize to NFKC and strip zero-width controls first.

kevin: rollout plan: 1) keep kv-resume disabled for cinder-int4 on canary; 2) enable merge-validator canary flag -> 24h at 5% -> if semantic-arg-order <1% promote; 3) revert or re-enable kv-resume only after merging tokenizer/decoder fixes upstream.

ops-bot: PRs: kv-resume toggle already deployed; merge-validator PR created at 1769999940.

tara: adding alert: semantic-arg-order > 1% triggers paging. Also adding a dashboard panel for array_mismatch_rate by model+quant.

kevin: good. let's also add a regression test that fuzzes arrays with nested objects so we don't accidentally overfit the validator.

mira: will add fuzz harness and run overnight. Posting here when results done.

tara: thanks all. will keep this thread updated; if fuzz finds anything alarming we'll freeze INT4 rollouts for cinder until resolved. :warning:
